parsed.explanation: No documented imprisonment, execution, organised sweeps or universal birth-sex facility rule for visitors, so not severe/high-risk levels. But combined regime is hostile and unremedied: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection, organisations unregistrable, expression censored and venues closed with rainbow display banned, and the only direct visitor evidence is May 2025 border mocking/questioning with no recourse. A narrow 2024 court payout and a 2018 guard dismissal show occasional recourse, not effective protection. Thin data on entry markers, facilities, custody and violence resolves toward structural hostility, not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: May 2025 visibly trans visitor laughed at, mocked and questioned by immigration officials; assessment anticipates derisive handling with no recourse mechanism.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Dependent residency for same-sex partners of residents is not a trans visitor document protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/appearance discrepancy can trigger border humiliation and outing before any court remedy is reachable.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No documented arrests, detention placement, searches or custody abuse for trans visitors in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Unknown placement or investigation practice remains an open risk if border encounter escalates; absence is not safety.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National censorship/broadcast baseline bans depictions of abnormal sexual behaviour and extends to platforms; rainbow items banned even in venues. University evidence shows sex-segregated facilities enforced by legal marker for residents.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented for visitors. No visitor facility-access protection documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National baseline applies across provinces; subnational variation is only procedural, not criminal/censorship baseline.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care heavily gated, adults need parental consent; online estradiol/androgen blocker sale banned Dec 2022 forcing in-person purchase; conversion practices remain routine in psychiatric facilities.
care_services.protection: Narrow protection: Nov 2024 record payout after electroshock conversion, first successful challenge. Seven youth centres, three offering blockers, are resident services.
care_services.interaction: Visitor medication continuity and emergency discovery occur inside a system centring family consent and conversion; no visitor care shield documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State censors LGBT content as disrupting social order, scrubs accounts/films/events around Pride 2026, cancelled famous trans dancer shows 2025, activism described as all but extinct.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. No anti-discrimination or hate-crime provisions; LGBTI organisations cannot register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing of queer expression as foreign ideology increases outing, police and border discretion risks without protective offset.

minors_guardians.exposure: Resident minors/adults face parental-consent gating for surgery and legal gender change, pushing disputes into families; one province alone allows minors to apply for marker change. No visitor-minor rule documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for travelling minors with guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor needing medication or care would encounter in-person-only, gated, family-consent system; specific visitor application uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single 2018 attack by security guards on women wearing rainbow badges in capital; no patterned trans-violence rate or background comparison documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Security company dismissed three guards shortly after 2018 attack.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dismissal shows occasional response but no hate-crime statute or documented pattern of prosecution for later incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No recourse for border mocking; courts exist narrowly, with first conversion win only in 2024 despite routine practice. Entry marker rules, screening, custody, ward placement and trans violence magnitude are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court payout in 2024 and 2018 dismissals are limited documented remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies do not correct censorship, border handling or care gating; unknowns cannot be counted as safety in this thin, hostile structural context.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-C? This case lacks documented repeated police stops, extortion and overnight detention of travellers. Border humiliation is documented once with anticipated recurrence, but not the organised police targeting of 0.35-C, so it rates above 0.35.

Similar to 0.45-C: no presentation offence, but widespread state suppression, no effective service remedy and thin recourse. Here discrimination prevalence is not surveyed and a conversion payout exists, keeping it near but slightly below the 0.45 anchor absent quantified visitor-facing denial.

Materially below 0.55-B: that anchor has mediators securing readmissions/refunds and police prosecution of assault. Here border abuse has no recourse, expression is nationally censored, and no anti-discrimination machinery is documented.

Well below 0.65-C: that anchor has documented social acceptance, dead-letter sexuality law with no use against gender-diverse people, and court compensation. Here acceptance is not documented as visitor protection, censorship is active, and travel-facing recourse is narrow.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime interaction: national censorship and no protective law frame the traveller as non-acceptable before arrival; border officials can humiliate with impunity; if outed in medical or sex-segregated settings, marker-tied practice and gated care apply with family-consent logic; courts offer only rare, narrow relief after harm. No tier-1 universal visitor ban or organised imprisonment is documented, preventing a 0.25-0.35 score, but unremedied state hostility and unresolved entry/custody unknowns prevent reduced-risk placement.
